film.title: The Transition
film.credit: Author, director and producer — Anastasia Kosheleva
film.synopsis: A dialogue-free work inspired by the inner experience of emigration during wartime. The film is built around Anastasia’s performance of Chopin’s Étude Op. 25 No. 12 and the visual contrast between warmth, isolation, movement, and a sense of liminal space.

biography.photoAlt: Anastasia Kosheleva at the piano, Kawai Thailand International Music Competition 2026
paragraphs: Anastasia Kosheleva is a Kyrgyzstani pianist, educator, composer and first-time film director whose creative practice develops at the intersection of music, visual language, and storytelling.

Classically trained as a pianist, she studied at the Gnessin Russian Academy of Music in Moscow, where she completed her higher musical education in 2020 and continued to develop her own artistic language through performance and interdisciplinary projects. During her studies, Anastasia was a recipient of the Scriabin Scholarship and became a laureate of international music competitions in Italy, the UAE, France, and countries across Asia.

Her career has taken her across many countries and cultures. As a pianist, Anastasia has performed and worked in France, Italy, China, Kyrgyzstan, Thailand, and the United Arab Emirates, developing her artistic thinking through constant interaction with different cultures, traditions, and forms of art.

Alongside her performing career, she has taught music for more than ten years. Her work has included individual lessons, masterclasses, and academic projects, while her own professional development continues through interaction with musicians, professors, and artists from different fields.

Anastasia’s musical repertoire spans works from the Baroque and Classical periods to Romanticism and twentieth-century music. She is particularly interested in composers whose music combines strict architectural form with deep psychological content. Alongside the classical repertoire, she develops her own musical projects and searches for contemporary visual forms of presenting music.

Gradually, her creative interests expanded beyond performance into photography, visual art, composition, and cinema. She does not view these areas as separate disciplines, but rather as different ways of expressing one inner idea. Her work often explores themes of atmosphere, memory, identity, displacement, and the interaction between sound and image.

In 2026, Anastasia made her debut as a director and producer with the experimental short film The Transition — a dialogue-free work inspired by the inner experience of emigration during wartime. The film is built around her performance of Chopin’s Étude Op. 25 No. 12 and the visual contrast between warmth, isolation, movement, and a sense of liminal space. This project became a continuation of her musical language through cinema and received international festival recognition, including official selections and awards.

Her visual approach is based on a desire to find the unusual in the everyday — transforming architecture, light, movement, accidental details, and fragments of ordinary life into atmospheric images. The same principle defines her work in music and cinema: instead of literally illustrating an idea, she searches for its emotional equivalent.

With family roots in Kyrgyzstan and professional experience of living and working in different countries, Anastasia sees cultural displacement not only as part of her biography, but also as an important element of her own artistic perspective.
Today, her practice brings together performance, composition, film, work with AI and teaching, forming a unified and constantly evolving artistic language.
